call_points.text: Reported utilisation is about 85%, but effective utilisation at several plants is close to full.
FY26 margin gain came from solar power, automation, yield and vendor renegotiation, not one-offs.
Replacement market grew 4% in FY26; company chose to focus more on OEMs.
Inventories fell by over ₹20 Cr at FY26 year-end even as sales rose.
Five-year revenue goal of ₹2,500 Cr is still aspirational but becoming concrete.
Management sees no internal risk; external geopolitics and supply chain are the main challenges.

entities.name: NRB Unitech Friction Solutions Private Limited

industry: Consumer Discretionary > Automobile and Auto Components > Auto Components > Auto Components & Equipments

operating_notes.text: FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin was 19.5%, up 118 bps from 18.3% in FY25, on volume growth, improved product mix and automation/energy cost initiatives.
Brownfield expansions at Jalna and Chikalthana are expected to start contributing from FY27.
Reported utilisation is roughly 85%, but effective utilisation at several plants is close to full.
Industrial business is approximately 14-15% of revenue, with a target of 20-25%.
Mahant Tool order book is close to ₹50 Cr, up from ₹25 Cr at acquisition, with HAL as the customer across divisions.

NRB Bearings holds 48,00,000 equity shares, or 8.50%, of Amplus Ampere Private Limited, falling to 5.93% after selling 2.57% to Apcotex Industries and Deepak Novochem Technologies for a combined ₹1.46 Cr.

timeline.summary: Harshbeena Sahney Zaveri declared no change in pledged shares under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4) as of April 2, 2026.
On May 7, 2026, NRB Bearing reported FY26 standalone revenue of ₹1,185.70 Cr, PAT of ₹121.51 Cr, declared a ₹2.25 interim dividend, and approved ₹40 Cr land acquisition.

On May 8, 2026, NRB Bearings' press release reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹1,335 Cr (+11% YoY), EBITDA of ₹267 Cr (+19%) and PAT of ₹146 Cr (+77%), with Jalna and Chikalthana brownfield expansions expected to contribute from FY27.

On May 11, 2026, NRB Bearings' Q4FY26 call guided FY27 capex at close to ₹120 Cr within a ₹240 Cr programme and international business growth at 10-14%, with brownfield commissioning from June-July 2026.
